### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Marden-Walker syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.747)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:26270)

**Proposed mechanism:** PIEZO2 (HGNC:26270) —DISRUPTS→ Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal and nervous systems (REACT:9811272); Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal and nervous systems (REACT:9811272) —LEADS_TO→ Scoliosis (HP:0002670); Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal and nervous systems (REACT:9811272) —LEADS_TO→ Contractures of the fingers and toes (HP:0002761); Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal and nervous systems (REACT:9811272) —LEADS_TO→ Muscular hypotonia (HP:0001252); Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal and nervous systems (REACT:9811272) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial shape (HP:0001999); Mechanotransduction in musculoskeletal and nervous systems (REACT:9811272) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebral hypomyelination (HP:0033736). Haploinsufficiency of PIEZO2 disrupts mechanotransduction, leading to overlapping phenotypes in both Gordon syndrome and Marden-Walker syndrome, including scoliosis, contractures, hypotonia, abnormal facial shape, and cerebral hypomyelination.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PIEZO2 associated with loss-of-function in both diseases, or conversely, evidence that distinct pathways are affected by PIEZO2 variants in each disease. _(variant: rs141880589)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PIEZO2 in these distinct syndromes opens avenues for targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating mechanosensory pathways, potentially benefiting patients with either Gordon syndrome or Marden-Walker syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in PIEZO2 in individuals with Gordon syndrome (MONDO:0007252) and arthrogryposis, distal, with impaired proprioception and touch (MONDO:0014941) would support this hypothesis.
